1.explanation:
The root of the bug is that plane (root) changes caused by either the modeling command (UpdateCanvasRootHandler.execute) or the drilldown button (DrilldownOverlayBehavior.addOverlay invoking canvas.setRootElement) do not notify the direct‐editing module to shut down the input. LabelEditingProvider wires up directEditing.complete()/cancel() on many interactions (canvas.viewbox.changing, drag.init, commandStack.changed, etc.) but never on canvas root changes. To fix the bug one must either:

• Add a listener in LabelEditingProvider (in its constructor) for the canvas root change event (e.g. eventBus.on('canvas.setRoot', …)) to call directEditing.complete() or cancel().

• Or, in UpdateCanvasRootHandler.execute (and revert) and/or DrilldownOverlayBehavior.addOverlay, explicitly invoke directEditing.cancel() (or complete()) before or after calling canvas.setRootElement.

These three classes/functions are directly responsible for switching the plane or providing direct editing, and thus are the points to hook in the cancellation logic.
1.bug_scenario: When editing a label inside a collapsed subprocess (i.e. on a non‐root plane), then drilling down into that subprocess (or executing a modeling command that switches the canvas root), the direct‐editing input box remains open even though the element being edited is no longer visible. The expected behavior is that direct editing is canceled or completed whenever the canvas root (plane) changes.

2.explanation:
• LabelEditingProvider (in lib/features/label-editing/LabelEditingProvider.js) is responsible for registering cancellation handlers when certain canvas or modeling events occur (e.g. canvas.viewbox.changing, drag.init, commandStack.changed) and for activating direct editing. However, it does not listen for canvas root changes, so when the plane is switched via drilldown the direct‐editing session isn’t cancelled.

• DrilldownOverlayBehavior (in lib/features/drilldown/DrilldownOverlayBehavior.js) wires up the drill‐down arrow button. Its addOverlay() method attaches a click handler that calls canvas.setRootElement(...) to change the plane, but this operation bypasses the existing direct‐editing cancellation hooks.

• UpdateCanvasRootHandler (in lib/features/modeling/cmd/UpdateCanvasRootHandler.js) implements the low‐level logic for swapping the canvas root element (execute()), but it does not emit an event or otherwise notify directEditing to cancel. 

To fix the bug, LabelEditingProvider needs to hook into the plane‐switch operation (e.g. listen for canvas.setRootElement or a canvas.root.changed event) and call directEditing.cancel() when the root element changes.
2.bug_scenario: In the provided GIF and diagram scenario, a label on a BPMN element is put into direct‐editing mode (the little text box appears for inline renaming). While that editing box is open, the user drills down into another plane (e.g. a collapsed subprocess) by clicking the drill‐down arrow. Although the canvas root is switched and the diagram “navigates” to the subprocess, the direct‐editing widget remains visible and active on the old plane (even though that element is no longer visible). The expected behavior is that changing planes should cancel any active direct editing.
